Copyright policy

Found your work on AutoStacc without your permission? Here's how to report it, how creators can answer a report, and what repeat infringement costs an account.

What this covers

Anything people upload or publish on AutoStacc: creators' products and packs, preview clips, creator pages and their images and fonts, shared site templates and reviews. AutoStacc respects copyright and expects everyone who uploads to have the rights to what they share (terms).

Reporting infringement

If you own the copyright in something on AutoStacc (or act for the owner), write to Email support@autostacc.com. with:

  • your name, postal address, phone number and email;
  • the work you own, and the AutoStacc address (link) of each thing you say infringes it;
  • a statement that you believe in good faith the use isn't authorised by the owner, its agent or the law;
  • a statement that the information in your notice is accurate and, under penalty of perjury, that you are the owner or authorised to act for them;
  • your physical or electronic signature (typing your full name is enough).

AutoStacc removes or disables what a complete notice points to promptly and tells the person who uploaded it, with a copy of the notice. Sending a notice you know is false can make you liable for damages.

If your upload was removed

If you believe it was removed by mistake or you have the rights to it, you can send a counter-notice to Email support@autostacc.com. with:

  • your name, address, phone number and email;
  • what was removed and where it was;
  • a statement, under penalty of perjury, that you believe in good faith it was removed by mistake or misidentification;
  • your consent to the jurisdiction of the federal court for your address (or, outside the United States, any court where AutoStacc may be found), and that you'll accept service from the person who sent the notice;
  • your signature.

AutoStacc passes the counter-notice to the person who sent the notice. Unless they tell AutoStacc within 10 to 14 business days that they've gone to court, the content is put back.

Repeat infringement

A notice that leads to a removal and isn't successfully answered by a counter-notice is a strike against the account that uploaded it, and half a strike against the creator space it was uploaded for (a whole one if the space's owner uploaded it, or if nobody else can be named). Each strike expires 12 months after it was given.

  • 1 strike: a warning.
  • 2 strikes: for an account, it can't publish or price products in any creator space; for a creator space, its products can't be bought or claimed free for now. You can answer a strike, or fix or remove the content and ask for selling back.
  • 3 strikes: the account can no longer sell, upload files or use the Studio. In serious cases AutoStacc may keep this in place after strikes expire.

Strikes never take away what you bought: you can always buy, download and use your purchases. The one exception is a file removed because a valid notice named it: nobody can download that file any more, and the people who bought it can get a refund for that product.

If you bought something that was removed

If a product you paid for is removed for infringement, see the refund policy.

Contact

Copyright notices and counter-notices: Email support@autostacc.com.
